q: 1. The flow in a pipe or channel is said to be uniform when
options: the liquid particles at all sections have the same velocities
the liquid particles at different sections have different velocities
explain: Uniform flow is defined by velocity (and other flow parameters) remaining constant with respect to distance along the flow path.

q: 2. A flow through an expanding tube at constant rate is called
explain: It is steady (constant rate), but non-uniform because the expanding area causes velocity to change along the length.

q: 3. A flow whose streamline is represented by a curve, is called
explain: When flow velocity is a function of two space coordinates (e.g., x and y), the streamlines become curves in a plane.

q: 4. In one dimensional flow, the flow
explain: The key characteristic is that the flow parameters only change along the direction of flow, which is typically a straight line path.

q: 5. The total head of a liquid particle in motion is equal to
options: pressure head + kinetic head + potential head
explain: Total head (H) = P/w + v²/2g + Z. It represents the energy per unit weight of the fluid.

q: 6. For a perfect incompressible liquid, flowing in a continuous stream, the total energy of a particle remains the same... This statement is called
explain: This is the core definition of Bernoulli's theorem for ideal fluid flow.

q: 7. Bernoulli's equation is applied to
explain: All three listed devices work by measuring pressure/velocity changes based on Bernoulli's principle.

q: 8. When the flow in an open channel is gradually varied, the flow is said to be ............
explain: Gradually Varied Flow (GVF) is a type of steady non-uniform flow where the depth of flow changes gradually along the length of the channel.

q: 9. The tangential velocity of the water element having a free vortex is ............
options: directly proportional to its distance from the centre
inversely proportional to its distance from the centre
directly proportional to its (distance)^2 from the centre
inversely proportional to its (distance)^2 from the centre
explain: In a free vortex, the velocity $v$ is inversely proportional to the radius $r$ ($vr = constant$).

q: 10. A flow in which ............ force is dominating over the viscosity is called turbulent flow.
explain: Turbulent flow is characterized by high inertia forces that overcome the damping effect of viscosity.

q: 11. When the mach number is between ............... the flow is called super-sonic flow.
explain: Supersonic flow occurs when 1 < Mach number < 6. Beyond M=6, the flow is typically classified as hypersonic.

q: 12. When the Mach number is more than 6, the flow is called ...............
explain: Flows with a Mach number greater than 5 or 6 are characterized by high temperature and dissociation effects, known as hyper-sonic flow.

q: 13. A flow is called super-sonic if the ...............
options: velocity of flow is very high
explain: Super-sonic flow is specifically defined by a Mach number greater than 1 but less than the hypersonic threshold (typically 6).

q: 14. A flow is called hyper-sonic, if the Mach number is ...............
explain: Since hyper-sonic flow requires a Mach number > 6, none of the specific ranges (M<1, M=1, or 1<M<6) apply.

q: 15. The ratio of the inertia force to the elastic force is called ...............
explain: The Mach number can also be defined as the square root of the ratio of inertia force to elastic force in a fluid.

q: 16. In fluids, steady, flow occurs when ...............
options: conditions of flow change steadily with time
conditions of flow do not change with time at a point
conditions of flow remain the same at adjacent point
velocity vector remains constant at a point
explain: Steady flow is defined as the type of flow in which the fluid properties (velocity, pressure, etc.) at any point do not change with time.

q: 17. A non-uniform steady flow is through ...............
options: a long tube at a decreasing rate
an expanding tube at constant rate
an expanding tube at increasing rate
a long pipe at increasing rate
explain: It is non-uniform because the cross-section changes (expanding tube) and steady because the discharge rate remains constant over time.

q: 18. Equation of continuity of fluids is applicable only if ...............
options: flow is steady and velocity is uniform
explain: While general forms exist, the standard engineering version (A1V1 = A2V2) assumes steady, one-dimensional, and usually incompressible flow.

q: 19. For the two dimensional flow, the stream functions is given by Ψ = 2xy. The velocity at a point (3, 4) is ...............
explain: u = -∂Ψ/∂y = -2x = -6; v = ∂Ψ/∂x = 2y = 8. Resultant velocity V = √(u² + v²) = √((-6)² + 8²) = 10 m/sec.

q: 20. The flow is called rotational if its velocity normal to the plane of area is equal to ...............
explain: Vorticity is defined as the curl of the velocity vector, which is equal to twice the angular velocity (ω).

q: 21. If the forces are due to inertia and gravity, and frictional resistance plays only a minor role, the design of the channels is made by comparing ...............
explain: Froude number is used for open channel designs where gravity is the primary driving force (e.g., spillways, canals).

q: 22. The phenomenon occurring in an open channel when a rapidly flowing stream abruptly changes to slowly flowing stream causing rise in water surface ...............
explain: A hydraulic jump occurs when supercritical flow (high velocity) transitions to subcritical flow (low velocity), resulting in significant energy dissipation and a rise in water level.

q: 23. The gases are considered incompressible when mach number ...............
explain: Gas flow is generally treated as incompressible if the Mach number is less than about 0.3, as density variations are negligible below this speed.

q: 24. The necessary condition for the flow to be steady is that
options: the velocity does not change from place to place
the velocity is constant at a point with respect to time
the velocity changes at a point with respect to time
explain: Steady flow is defined as the type of flow in which fluid characteristics like velocity, pressure, and density at a point do not change with time (dv/dt = 0).

q: 25. Bernoulli's equation is derived making assumptions that
options: the flow is uniform, steady and incompressible
the flow is non-viscous, uniform and steady
the flow is steady, non-viscous, incompressible and irrotational
explain: The standard derivation of Bernoulli's equation assumes the fluid is ideal (non-viscous), the flow is steady, incompressible, and occurs along a streamline (irrotational).

q: 26. If the velocity, pressure, density etc, do not change at a point with respect to time, the flow is called
explain: When fluid properties at a specific point remain constant regardless of time, the flow is categorized as steady flow.

q: 27. The term V²/2g is known as
explain: In the Bernoulli equation, the term V²/2g represents the Kinetic Head, which is the kinetic energy of the fluid per unit weight.

q: 28. The loss of pressure head for the laminar flow through pipes varies
options: as the inverse of the velocity
explain: According to the Hagen-Poiseuille equation for laminar flow, the head loss (hf) is given by (32μVL)/(ρgD²). This shows that head loss is directly proportional to the first power of the velocity (V).

q: 29. The value of the kinetic energy correction factor (α) for the viscous flow through a circular pipe is
explain: The kinetic energy correction factor (α) accounts for the non-uniform velocity distribution. For laminar (viscous) flow in a circular pipe, α is equal to 2.0.

q: 30. The value of the momentum correction factor (β) for the viscous flow through a circular pipe is
explain: The momentum correction factor (β) for laminar flow in a circular pipe is calculated as 4/3, which is approximately 1.33.

q: 31. Models are known undistorted model, if
options: prototype and model have different scale ratios
prototype and model have same scale ratio
model and prototype are kinematically similar
explain: An undistorted model is one that is geometrically similar to its prototype, meaning the scale ratio for all linear dimensions (length, width, height) is the same.

q: 32. Geometric similarity between model and prototype means
explain: Geometric similarity exists when the ratio of all corresponding linear dimensions in the model and prototype are equal.

q: 33. Kinematic similarity between model and prototype means
explain: Kinematic similarity means the similarity of motion; it occurs when the ratios of velocities and accelerations at corresponding points in the model and prototype are equal.

q: 34. Mach number (M) is given by
explain: The Mach number is the ratio of the local flow velocity (V) to the local speed of sound (C) in that medium.

q: 35. A body is called stream-lined body when it is placed in a flow and the surface
options: does not coincide with the streamlines
explain: A streamlined body is shaped such that its surface aligns with the streamlines of the flow, minimizing separation and pressure drag.

q: 36. The skin friction drag on a sphere (for Reynolds number less than 0.2) is equal to
explain: In Stokes' flow (Re < 0.2), the total drag is 6πηrv. Mathematically, 2/3 of this is due to skin friction and 1/3 is due to pressure.

q: 37. The pressure drag on a sphere (for Reynolds number less than 0.2) is equal to
explain: As derived in Stokes' law, for very low Reynolds numbers, pressure drag accounts for exactly one-third of the total resistance force.

q: 38. If the depth of flow along the length of the channel is a variable, then flow is known as
explain: Non-uniform flow (or varied flow) occurs when the depth of flow changes from one section to another along the channel.

q: 39. If the velocity at a section of a channel is variable with respect to time, then the flow in the channel is known as
explain: Unsteady flow occurs when fluid properties at a section change over time.
